brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix extend Tuesday's -14% rout on China WFE fears; HBM shortage persists through 2027, CoWoS easing Q4
brief.summary: <cite index="39-9,39-10,39-11">SK Hynix fell >8% intraday Wednesday after Tuesday's -14.7% plunge; Samsung dropped ~5% following -14.4% prior session. KOSPI sank 10.84% Tuesday.</cite> <cite index="43-2,43-7">SOX entered bear market (-20% from June peak) on unverified report that Chinese state-backed firm began mass-producing domestic chipmaking equipment.</cite> <cite index="39-12">SK Hynix Q2 revenue 79.32T won, operating profit 60.54T won—both records, both missed consensus.</cite> <cite index="8-2,8-3,8-13">HBM3E capacity pre-sold for 2026; top three memory makers allocated full HBM output; Micron Q2 2026 gross margin 68%.</cite> <cite index="30-10">CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026, improving further in 2027.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix held 57% global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%.</cite> <cite index="5-3">UBS expects SK Hynix to maintain ~50% HBM market share in 2026.</cite> Relative: Long SK Hynix vs. short Samsung. <cite index="39-3,39-4">SK Hynix has record HBM4 mass shipments and multi-year agreements with ~10 major customers; selloff is 'missed consensus' vs. fundamentals.</cite> <cite index="2-4">Samsung is 'struggling with the technology'</cite> and <cite index="5-4">nearing HBM3E qualification, with possible pricing pushback.</cite> Samsung's HBM lag + foundry/logic dilution widens the performance delta; SK Hynix pure-play leverage to AI memory justifies premium despite near-term compression.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-2,13-9">TrendForce projects global memory market at $551.6B in 2026, DRAM revenue up 144% YoY at $404.3B.</cite> <cite index="8-11">Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026, NAND +45%, ASPs climbing >30%.</cite> <cite index="15-2">Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices projected +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%—cooling from ~60% Q2 jumps.</cite> <cite index="45-4,45-5">Broker reports cite memory price peak in 2027; Standard Chartered expects prices to peak next year.</cite> <cite index="11-7,11-8">Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron permanently redirected wafer production toward HBM for AI data centers, removing supply from consumer market amid open-ended hyperscaler purchase commitments.</cite> <cite index="11-10">Meaningful price relief not expected until late 2027 or early 2028, when new fabs reach volume production.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments projected +35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb.</cite> <cite index="8-2,8-12,8-13">HBM3E dominant AI memory through 2026, pricing power intact until new capacity after 2027; capacity pre-sold, Micron Q2 2026 gross margin 68%.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historically.</cite> <cite index="5-7">SK Hynix expects only 'minimal to modest downtick' in HBM3E pricing for 2026 vs. 2025.</cite> <cite index="13-1">Counterpoint: DDR4 spot prices ($2.10/Gbit) now exceed HBM3e contract prices ($1.70/Gbit).</cite> <cite index="1-5">Micron integrating HBM3E 36GB 12-high into AMD Instinct MI350 Series.</cite> <cite index="1-6,1-7">AMD MI400 features 12 HBM4 stacks, 432GB on-package memory, ~19.6 TB/s bandwidth; early HBM4 modules deliver ~1.6 TB/s each.</cite>

key_filings.summary_en: Q2 2026 operating profit topped estimates on sustained AI-driven memory chip demand
Q2 2026 record revenue 79.32T won, operating profit 60.54T won; both missed analyst estimates despite records

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix, Samsung extend selloff: -14.7%/-14.4% Tue, -8%/-5% Wed on China WFE report
news_pulse.implication: Unverified report of Chinese state-backed firm mass-producing domestic chipmaking equipment triggered SOX bear market (-20% from June peak). Pure sentiment-driven; no change to HBM fundamentals or hyperscaler capex outlook.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 AI capex: $660-725B aggregate (Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, MSFT ~$120B, Oracle $50B)
news_pulse.implication: Up 77% YoY from $410B in 2025. Supply-constrained, not demand-constrained. Structural bid for HBM/DRAM continues; validates memory pricing power through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: HBM capacity pre-sold for 2026; top 3 memory makers allocated full output; Micron Q2 2026 gross margin 68%
news_pulse.implication: Zero-sum game: every HBM wafer denies LPDDR5X/consumer DRAM. Gross margin delta (68% HBM vs. <40% legacy) explains PC/smartphone memory deprioritization. Reinforces Samsung/SK Hynix pricing power.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026, improving 2027
news_pulse.implication: TSMC CoWoS capacity reaching 115-140K wpm end-2026, ~170K wpm 2027. Advanced packaging bottleneck easing ahead of HBM supply relief; GPU supply improves Q4, lifting memory attach rates.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot $2.10/Gbit now exceeds HBM3e contract $1.70/Gbit; DRAM revenue +144% YoY to $404.3B
news_pulse.implication: Commodity DRAM pricing inversion vs. premium HBM signals acute consumer supply shortage. Spot buyers paying more for DDR4 than hyperscalers for HBM3e underscores AI-driven capacity reallocation severity.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%—cooling from ~60% Q2 gains as consumers hit affordability ceiling
news_pulse.implication: Sequential gains decelerating due to demand destruction, not supply relief. AI/enterprise demand intact; consumer elasticity breaking. Mix shift toward HBM/server DRAM accelerates margin expansion for Samsung/SK Hynix.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q2 revenue 79.32T won, OP 60.54T won—records but missed consensus; market punishing 'expectations miss' not fundamentals
news_pulse.implication: Record HBM4 mass shipments + multi-year agreements with ~10 major customers confirm AI-memory demand sticky. Selloff creates entry; any confirmation HBM pricing/shipments hold triggers mean reversion.

news_pulse.headline: Sequoia's Cahn: ~$600B annual revenue gap between hyperscaler AI spending and ecosystem sales; Allianz: capex-revenue divergence 46% vs. 32% in 2001 telecom bubble
news_pulse.implication: Rising ROI skepticism and capex fatigue risk. However, AWS running $150B annualized +28% YoY, Google Cloud +63% Q1. Binary outcome: AI scales profitably or capex cuts. Memory suppliers insulated by LTAs; hyperscaler credit spreads (Oracle CDS 3x since Sep) more vulnerable.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures positioning reset post-10.84% Tuesday drawdown; implied vol elevated. Samsung/SK Hynix ADR-to-local discount widened intraday Wednesday, normalizing by close. Flow suggests capitulation complete if no fresh China WFE confirmation surfaces; watch Friday options expiry for gamma unwind. CoWoS easing + hyperscaler capex confirmation (MSFT/GOOGL earnings next week) could trigger short squeeze.
